title: Styles
description: The dance-floor styles the app teaches. Each move belongs to one. Shown in this order.

id.description: Stable short id. Moves and saved settings refer to it, so never change or reuse one that has shipped.

description.description: One or two sentences on what the style feels like.

bpm.description: Typical tempo range in beats per minute, and where the practice beat starts for this style.

default.description: Tempo the practice beat starts at.

music.description: Genres you'd hear this style danced to.

why.description: Optional: something about the style that isn't obvious and helps people get it.

groove.description: Optional: the practice beat's music for this style, played by synthesised drums, bass and keys. Without one, the beat is a plain click. Each lane loops on its own length in 16th-note steps (16 steps = one bar), so a lane can be 1, 2 or 4 bars long.

name.description: Shown next to the beat while it plays, like "Post-punk groove".

root.description: Key note as a MIDI number (40 is E, 45 is A). Bass plays at this pitch; lead, pad and notes are semitones above it.

lead.description: A melody an octave above the bass.

pad.description: Held chords, one per bar, as semitones above the root (played two octaves up). Loops.

drive.description: How much the bass is distorted.

lead.description: Lead voice. acid is a squelchy filtered sawtooth.

echo.description: How much echo the snare, toms, lead and pad get.

drums.description: One character per 16th-note step: x loud hit, o normal hit, . rest.

notes.description: Space-separated 16th-note steps: a number is a note that many semitones above the root, - is a rest, ~ holds the note before.
